events.text: Diagnosed against the live resident model with Agent Seat, without mutation. The selected two authored faces are real exterior faces: X-Ray is off, their shown normal points roughly +Y, and the current face-to-camera vector is on that front side (dot about 0.194). mesh_audit does not test actual raster visibility or the current camera. It casts only 42 Fibonacci-sphere directions from each triangle centroid +0.1mm normal offset, limited to the normal-facing hemisphere. For the live pose the nearest eligible synthetic direction is about 15.77 degrees from the actual visible camera ray, so a narrow slit can be visibly open while every sampled ray is blocked. The selector faithfully selects the audit marks; deleting those triangles proves the marks refer to real faces, not that the sampled classification was correct.

resolution: Diagnosed the two visibly exterior faces as a reachability-audit false positive. The audit samples 42 fixed directions from one point—the triangle centroid offset 0.1 mm along its normal—and never tests the current camera ray. In the live non-X-Ray pose, the camera sees the selected faces from their front side, but the nearest audit sample is about 15.8 degrees away, enough to miss the narrow escape corridor between surrounding geometry. Audit selection is internally consistent with its marks, which is why Delete affects the highlighted real faces; the classification itself is wrong here.
